currentContext.strengths: Three-location manufacturing footprint - Daman (UT), Roorkee (Uttarakhand) and Palsana (Surat-Gujrat) - stated in the Company Overview note|Quality, environment and occupational-health certifications maintained: 'the Company also upheld its commitment to quality and safety by maintaining certifications for ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001'|Raw-material supply security claimed: 'The Company has long term raw material supply MOU's and majority suppliers of the Company are regular in nature'|Receivable protection across the whole book: 'all domestic and export sales are protected by a receivable insurance policy, providing further security against payment defaults'|Captive renewable power - additional 5.2 MW solar capacity installed in FY26, stated to reduce dependence on conventional electricity and lower energy cost|In-house laboratory and testing capability, which the Directors' Report says FY26 capex was partly directed at ('laboratory and testing facilities')|496 people on the rolls of the Company as at FY 2025-26 (MD&A Human Resource section)
currentContext.strategies: Stay a single-segment masterbatch manufacturer - the MD&A states 'Your Company operates in one segment only - Masterbatches' - while shifting mix toward value-added and specialised applications where technical expertise and quality consistency differentiate.|Strengthen the product portfolio and expand customer relationships, with emphasis on innovative solutions that address evolving market requirements (MD&A Business Outlook).|Improve operational excellence and operating efficiency, explicitly linked in the Directors' Report to cost optimization measures being implemented against escalated raw-material rates and a weakening rupee.|Invest in manufacturing infrastructure to support long-term growth - FY26 capital expenditure was directed at expansion of the Engineering plastics plant, masterbatch capacity enhancement, laboratory and testing facilities, renewable energy projects and other infrastructure improvements.|Reduce energy cost and carbon footprint through captive renewable energy, having added 5.2 MW of solar capacity in FY26 to raise the renewable share of total power consumption.|Develop value-added masterbatch solutions aimed at the packaging, automotive, agriculture, consumer goods and infrastructure sectors (the sectors the Directors' Report names as the target of the FY26 capex).|Dividend is governed by a formal, published Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations; the Directors' Report states the Board 'while taking decision for recommendation of the dividend will take guidance from this policy and would ensure to maintain a positive approach to dividend payout plans', and the policy is hosted on the Company's website. For FY26 the Board recommended a dividend of ` 3.00 per share (60% on the ` 5.00 face value), placed before the 35th AGM on 24 August 2026 as ordinary business; the prior year's payout was ` 2.50 per share (50%), so the stated intent of a rising payout was acted on. Reserves policy is to make no appropriation at all - 'The Board of Directors have decided to retain the entire amount of profits for F.Y. 2025-26 in the Profit & Loss Account.' Reinvestment intent is stated in the same report as strategic capital expenditure to strengthen manufacturing infrastructure and support long-term growth (engineering plastics, masterbatch capacity, laboratory and testing, renewable energy), plus captive solar to reduce energy cost. Unclaimed dividends up to FY 2017-18 have been transferred to the IEPF and the corresponding shares are to follow. No buyback, no debt-reduction target and no credit rating is mentioned anywhere in the routed text. (Dividend-policy, reserves and reinvestment sentences are back-filled from the Directors' Report in sibling bundles; the AGM dividend resolution and the cost-auditor item are from the Notice of AGM in this bundle.)|Captive renewable energy expansion: 'Company continued its commitment towards environmental sustainability by augmenting its captive renewable energy portfolio through the installation of additional 5.2 MW solar power capacity' - stated to increase the renewable share of overall power consumption, reduce dependence on conventional electricity and lower the carbon footprint. This is the only quantified environmental action in the routed text, and it is an achieved FY26 action rather than a forward target.|Renewable energy is embedded in the asset base to the extent that 'Solar Generation System' is a named property, plant and equipment category with its own useful life in the accounting policy note (back-filled from the sibling profile/registry bundles).|Certifications maintained through FY 2025-26 for ISO 9001 (quality), ISO 14001 (environment) and ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety) - the Company frames these as its dedication to operational excellence and to occupational health and safety standards. NOTE: this bundle's MD&A is cut off mid-list at 'ISO 9001, ISO 14001'; ISO 45001 is back-filled from the identical sentence in the sibling profile bundle.|Employee health, safety and welfare: health check-up camps organised during FY 2025-26, and continued coverage under Group Term Life Insurance, Group Mediclaim Insurance and Group Personal Accident Insurance; employee recognition programmes, regular feedback sessions and performance evaluations; 496 people on the rolls of the Company (back-filled from the sibling profile bundle, whose MD&A extends past this bundle's cut).|Governance-side ESG: risk management is delegated by the Board to a Risk Management Committee whose framework is periodically evaluated by the Board, and a comprehensive data-protection policy plus enterprise-wide compliance management system are in place.|The Company acknowledges the sector-level sustainability shift - regulatory focus on plastic-waste management, recycling and the circular economy driving 'recyclable materials, recycled polymer applications, biodegradable solutions, and environmentally responsible manufacturing processes' - but states this as an industry trend and an opportunity, NOT as a commitment of its own; no recycled-content, emissions, energy-intensity, water or waste target is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, and no BRSR section is present in this bundle.
currentContext.expansion: FY26 was a maintenance-plus-debottlenecking year rather than a new-plant year. The Directors' Report states the Company 'undertook strategic capital expenditure to the extent of Rs. 2,433 Lakhs to strengthen its manufacturing infrastructure and support its long-term growth strategy', spread across five named buckets: expansion of the Engineering plastics plant, masterbatch capacity enhancement, laboratory and testing facilities, renewable energy projects, and other infrastructure improvements. No site is named against any of these buckets and no incremental capacity (MT per annum or otherwise) is quantified for any of them. Carry-over into FY27 is explicit: 'As on March 31, 2026, the Company has a capital work-in-progress of Rs. 615 Lakhs pertaining to capacity enhancement, which is expected to be completed and commissioned with in the next financial year' - i.e. commissioning is promised during FY27, again without a stated tonnage or location. On energy, the Company 'continued its commitment towards environmental sustainability by augmenting its captive renewable energy portfolio through the installation of additional 5.2 MW solar power capacity', which it expects to raise the renewable share of overall power consumption, cut dependence on conventional electricity and lower its carbon footprint; this is the only expansion item in the whole bundle with a quantified physical size. Existing footprint (from the Company Overview note in the sibling profile bundle) is three manufacturing facilities - Daman (UT), Roorkee (Uttarakhand) and Palsana (Surat-Gujrat). NO MASTERBATCH CAPACITY IS DISCLOSED: neither the MD&A nor the Directors' Report nor any BRSR block in the routed text states installed capacity in MT per annum, per plant or in total, for FY26 or any prior year, and no production or utilisation volume is given either - so installed_capacity is correctly empty rather than inferred from the capex narrative.
currentContext.mdna: Packaging is expected to remain the major growth driver, on demand from food processing, pharmaceuticals, personal care, beverages and e-commerce, with brand owners' focus on differentiation, visual appeal, functionality and sustainability driving demand for customised colour and additive masterbatches.|Automotive transformation - lightweighting, EV adoption, improved safety standards and higher aesthetic requirements - is expected to generate increased demand for specialised masterbatch products.|Growing polymer use in agriculture, healthcare, infrastructure, electrical and electronics, renewable energy and consumer applications is expected to further diversify demand.|Industry mix shift: the global masterbatch industry 'continues to evolve from being primarily a commodity-driven market toward a technology-oriented and application-focused industry', so specialty and high-performance grades are the growth pool while commodity grades face intense competition.|Indian demand support from rising polymer consumption, urbanisation, expanding manufacturing activity and government initiatives (Make in India, PLI, National Logistics Policy, PM Gati Shakti) plus infrastructure investment.|Regulatory-driven demand for sustainability: plastic-waste, recycling and circular-economy rules are accelerating industry adoption of recyclable materials, recycled polymer applications and biodegradable solutions.|Margin exposure runs through crude oil, polymer resin, pigment and additive costs; the Directors' Report adds that escalation in the West Asia conflict caused a significant rise in raw-material prices and that the FY26 one-time gain from holding minimum inventory 'shall not last long'.|Macro backdrop cited: IMF global growth of around 3.1% to 3.3% during 2026, and India's growth projected in the range of approximately 6.3% to 6.5%.|The Company describes itself as 'well positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities' on the strength of a diversified customer base, strong manufacturing capabilities and emphasis on quality and innovation, while remaining 'cautiously optimistic' on the long term given near-term external uncertainties.

risks.risk: Raw-material and feedstock price volatility (crude oil, polymer resin, pigments, additives, other petrochemical feedstocks)
risks.note: The MD&A states masterbatch manufacturers 'remain exposed to fluctuations in crude oil prices, polymer resin costs, pigment prices, additive costs, and other petrochemical feedstocks, which may impact profitability'. The Directors' Report makes it concrete for FY26: geopolitical factors caused wide fluctuation in raw-material prices and supply-chain disruptions, and 'Escalation in West Asia conflict resulted in significant rise in raw material prices'. Management adds that the year's one-time marginal gain from holding minimum inventory 'shall not last long' and that cost-optimization measures are being implemented - i.e. the input-cost tailwind is explicitly flagged as reversing.

'Your Company operates in one segment only - Masterbatches.' There is no second segment, no geographic segment disclosure and no customer-concentration disclosure to offset it, so every demand, price and regulatory shock in the masterbatch chain lands undiluted on the whole company.

risks.risk: Competition from organised and unorganised players, especially in commodity grades
risks.note: The MD&A says the industry 'faces competition from both organized and unorganized players, resulting in pricing pressures and margin challenges, particularly in commodity product segments', and that commodity-grade products 'continue to face intense competition' while differentiation sits in value-added and specialised applications. This is the structural argument for the Company's stated mix shift toward specialty grades.

risks.risk: Environmental and plastics regulation - waste management, recycling obligations, circular-economy requirements
risks.note: Flagged twice: the Indian-economy section cites 'increasing environmental regulations relating to plastic waste management and recycling', and the threats paragraph warns such requirements 'may necessitate additional investments and operational adjustments' - i.e. a potential forced-capex and compliance-cost risk on a plastics-chain business.

risks.risk: Currency risk on imported inputs, capital equipment and exports
risks.note: The MD&A says volatility in currency markets 'may impact the cost of imported raw materials and influence export competitiveness', and the Directors' Report cites a 'weakening rupee' among the pressures behind cost optimization. Note 49 states the exposure 'relates primarily to the import of raw materials and spare parts, capital expenditure, exports of finished products', with unhedged USD and Euro trade receivable/payable balances outstanding at the reporting date and a stated 1% sensitivity on profit before tax; the Company says it negotiates derivative terms to match hedged exposures where a hedge is entered into.

risks.risk: Credit risk from extended customer credit terms
risks.note: 'The Company faces credit risk through its extended credit terms to customers, which may result in payment delays or defaults.' Mitigations are unusually specific: regular monitoring of receivables and proactive collection, a credit-evaluation policy setting a limit per customer, bank guarantee / letter of credit / security deposit backing where credit risk is assessed as high, expected-credit-loss provisioning on a provision matrix, and - materially - 'all domestic and export sales are protected by a receivable insurance policy'. Trade receivables are stated to consist of a large number of customers.

Liquidity risk is described as the potential inability to meet short-term obligations from insufficient cash flow or limited access to financing, managed through cash-flow forecasting, maintained credit lines and working-capital optimisation across inventory, receivables and payables. On interest rates, Note 49 states market risk 'arises from the Company's use of interest bearing financial instruments' and that the instruments affected are borrowings; the borrowing table shows the reporting-date position as entirely floating-rate INR with no fixed-rate and no foreign-currency borrowing, and the Company discloses a 100 bps sensitivity - so the whole borrowing book reprices with rates.

risks.risk: Regulatory / statutory change and cyber risk
risks.note: Regulatory risk from changes in statutes, laws and regulations is managed through periodic legal-compliance reviews and an enterprise-wide compliance management system. Cyber risk - data breaches, cyber attacks or system failures - is addressed with a data-protection policy, encryption and firewalls, and information stored across multiple secure locations. Both sit under the Risk Management Committee, to which the Board has delegated review of the risk-management system in line with the Companies Act 2013 and SEBI Regulations.

risks.risk: Supplier dependence, partially offset by long-term supply arrangements
risks.note: The only 'Operational Issues' disclosure in the MD&A risk section is the mitigation itself: 'The Company has long term raw material supply MOU's and majority suppliers of the Company are regular in nature.' No supplier count, no concentration percentage and no named supplier is given, so the residual concentration cannot be sized from the report.

Amounts are deliberately not reproduced; the note is truncated after this single row.

demand_drivers.body:
- Packaging is expected to remain the major growth driver, on demand from food processing, pharmaceuticals, personal care, beverages and e-commerce, with brand owners' focus on differentiation, visual appeal, functionality and sustainability driving demand for customised colour and additive masterbatches.
- Automotive transformation - lightweighting, EV adoption, improved safety standards and higher aesthetic requirements - is expected to generate increased demand for specialised masterbatch products.
- Growing polymer use in agriculture, healthcare, infrastructure, electrical and electronics, renewable energy and consumer applications is expected to further diversify demand.
- Industry mix shift: the global masterbatch industry 'continues to evolve from being primarily a commodity-driven market toward a technology-oriented and application-focused industry', so specialty and high-performance grades are the growth pool while commodity grades face intense competition.
- Indian demand support from rising polymer consumption, urbanisation, expanding manufacturing activity and government initiatives (Make in India, PLI, National Logistics Policy, PM Gati Shakti) plus infrastructure investment.
- Regulatory-driven demand for sustainability: plastic-waste, recycling and circular-economy rules are accelerating industry adoption of recyclable materials, recycled polymer applications and biodegradable solutions.
- Margin exposure runs through crude oil, polymer resin, pigment and additive costs; the Directors' Report adds that escalation in the West Asia conflict caused a significant rise in raw-material prices and that the FY26 one-time gain from holding minimum inventory 'shall not last long'.
- Macro backdrop cited: IMF global growth of around 3.1% to 3.3% during 2026, and India's growth projected in the range of approximately 6.3% to 6.5%.
- The Company describes itself as 'well positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities' on the strength of a diversified customer base, strong manufacturing capabilities and emphasis on quality and innovation, while remaining 'cautiously optimistic' on the long term given near-term external uncertainties.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Stay a single-segment masterbatch manufacturer - the MD&A states 'Your Company operates in one segment only - Masterbatches' - while shifting mix toward value-added and specialised applications where technical expertise and quality consistency differentiate.
- Strengthen the product portfolio and expand customer relationships, with emphasis on innovative solutions that address evolving market requirements (MD&A Business Outlook).
- Improve operational excellence and operating efficiency, explicitly linked in the Directors' Report to cost optimization measures being implemented against escalated raw-material rates and a weakening rupee.
- Invest in manufacturing infrastructure to support long-term growth - FY26 capital expenditure was directed at expansion of the Engineering plastics plant, masterbatch capacity enhancement, laboratory and testing facilities, renewable energy projects and other infrastructure improvements.
- Reduce energy cost and carbon footprint through captive renewable energy, having added 5.2 MW of solar capacity in FY26 to raise the renewable share of total power consumption.
- Develop value-added masterbatch solutions aimed at the packaging, automotive, agriculture, consumer goods and infrastructure sectors (the sectors the Directors' Report names as the target of the FY26 capex).
- Dividend is governed by a formal, published Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations; the Directors' Report states the Board 'while taking decision for recommendation of the dividend will take guidance from this policy and would ensure to maintain a positive approach to dividend payout plans', and the policy is hosted on the Company's website. For FY26 the Board recommended a dividend of ` 3.00 per share (60% on the ` 5.00 face value), placed before the 35th AGM on 24 August 2026 as ordinary business; the prior year's payout was ` 2.50 per share (50%), so the stated intent of a rising payout was acted on. Reserves policy is to make no appropriation at all - 'The Board of Directors have decided to retain the entire amount of profits for F.Y. 2025-26 in the Profit & Loss Account.' Reinvestment intent is stated in the same report as strategic capital expenditure to strengthen manufacturing infrastructure and support long-term growth (engineering plastics, masterbatch capacity, laboratory and testing, renewable energy), plus captive solar to reduce energy cost. Unclaimed dividends up to FY 2017-18 have been transferred to the IEPF and the corresponding shares are to follow. No buyback, no debt-reduction target and no credit rating is mentioned anywhere in the routed text. (Dividend-policy, reserves and reinvestment sentences are back-filled from the Directors' Report in sibling bundles; the AGM dividend resolution and the cost-auditor item are from the Notice of AGM in this bundle.)
- Captive renewable energy expansion: 'Company continued its commitment towards environmental sustainability by augmenting its captive renewable energy portfolio through the installation of additional 5.2 MW solar power capacity' - stated to increase the renewable share of overall power consumption, reduce dependence on conventional electricity and lower the carbon footprint. This is the only quantified environmental action in the routed text, and it is an achieved FY26 action rather than a forward target.
- Renewable energy is embedded in the asset base to the extent that 'Solar Generation System' is a named property, plant and equipment category with its own useful life in the accounting policy note (back-filled from the sibling profile/registry bundles).
- Certifications maintained through FY 2025-26 for ISO 9001 (quality), ISO 14001 (environment) and ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety) - the Company frames these as its dedication to operational excellence and to occupational health and safety standards. NOTE: this bundle's MD&A is cut off mid-list at 'ISO 9001, ISO 14001'; ISO 45001 is back-filled from the identical sentence in the sibling profile bundle.
- Employee health, safety and welfare: health check-up camps organised during FY 2025-26, and continued coverage under Group Term Life Insurance, Group Mediclaim Insurance and Group Personal Accident Insurance; employee recognition programmes, regular feedback sessions and performance evaluations; 496 people on the rolls of the Company (back-filled from the sibling profile bundle, whose MD&A extends past this bundle's cut).
- Governance-side ESG: risk management is delegated by the Board to a Risk Management Committee whose framework is periodically evaluated by the Board, and a comprehensive data-protection policy plus enterprise-wide compliance management system are in place.
- The Company acknowledges the sector-level sustainability shift - regulatory focus on plastic-waste management, recycling and the circular economy driving 'recyclable materials, recycled polymer applications, biodegradable solutions, and environmentally responsible manufacturing processes' - but states this as an industry trend and an opportunity, NOT as a commitment of its own; no recycled-content, emissions, energy-intensity, water or waste target is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, and no BRSR section is present in this bundle.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was a maintenance-plus-debottlenecking year rather than a new-plant year. The Directors' Report states the Company 'undertook strategic capital expenditure to the extent of Rs. 2,433 Lakhs to strengthen its manufacturing infrastructure and support its long-term growth strategy', spread across five named buckets: expansion of the Engineering plastics plant, masterbatch capacity enhancement, laboratory and testing facilities, renewable energy projects, and other infrastructure improvements. No site is named against any of these buckets and no incremental capacity (MT per annum or otherwise) is quantified for any of them. Carry-over into FY27 is explicit: 'As on March 31, 2026, the Company has a capital work-in-progress of Rs. 615 Lakhs pertaining to capacity enhancement, which is expected to be completed and commissioned with in the next financial year' - i.e. commissioning is promised during FY27, again without a stated tonnage or location. On energy, the Company 'continued its commitment towards environmental sustainability by augmenting its captive renewable energy portfolio through the installation of additional 5.2 MW solar power capacity', which it expects to raise the renewable share of overall power consumption, cut dependence on conventional electricity and lower its carbon footprint; this is the only expansion item in the whole bundle with a quantified physical size. Existing footprint (from the Company Overview note in the sibling profile bundle) is three manufacturing facilities - Daman (UT), Roorkee (Uttarakhand) and Palsana (Surat-Gujrat). NO MASTERBATCH CAPACITY IS DISCLOSED: neither the MD&A nor the Directors' Report nor any BRSR block in the routed text states installed capacity in MT per annum, per plant or in total, for FY26 or any prior year, and no production or utilisation volume is given either - so installed_capacity is correctly empty rather than inferred from the capex narrative.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Three-location manufacturing footprint - Daman (UT), Roorkee (Uttarakhand) and Palsana (Surat-Gujrat) - stated in the Company Overview note
- Quality, environment and occupational-health certifications maintained: 'the Company also upheld its commitment to quality and safety by maintaining certifications for ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001'
- Raw-material supply security claimed: 'The Company has long term raw material supply MOU's and majority suppliers of the Company are regular in nature'
- Receivable protection across the whole book: 'all domestic and export sales are protected by a receivable insurance policy, providing further security against payment defaults'
- Captive renewable power - additional 5.2 MW solar capacity installed in FY26, stated to reduce dependence on conventional electricity and lower energy cost
- In-house laboratory and testing capability, which the Directors' Report says FY26 capex was partly directed at ('laboratory and testing facilities')
- 496 people on the rolls of the Company as at FY 2025-26 (MD&A Human Resource section)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw-material and feedstock price volatility (crude oil, polymer resin, pigments, additives, other petrochemical feedstocks) — The MD&A states masterbatch manufacturers 'remain exposed to fluctuations in crude oil prices, polymer resin costs, pigment prices, additive costs, and other petrochemical feedstocks, which may impact profitability'. The Directors' Report makes it concrete for FY26: geopolitical factors caused wide fluctuation in raw-material prices and supply-chain disruptions, and 'Escalation in West Asia conflict resulted in significant rise in raw material prices'. Management adds that the year's one-time marginal gain from holding minimum inventory 'shall not last long' and that cost-optimization measures are being implemented - i.e. the input-cost tailwind is explicitly flagged as reversing.
- Single-segment, single-product concentration — 'Your Company operates in one segment only - Masterbatches.' There is no second segment, no geographic segment disclosure and no customer-concentration disclosure to offset it, so every demand, price and regulatory shock in the masterbatch chain lands undiluted on the whole company.
- Competition from organised and unorganised players, especially in commodity grades — The MD&A says the industry 'faces competition from both organized and unorganized players, resulting in pricing pressures and margin challenges, particularly in commodity product segments', and that commodity-grade products 'continue to face intense competition' while differentiation sits in value-added and specialised applications. This is the structural argument for the Company's stated mix shift toward specialty grades.
- Environmental and plastics regulation - waste management, recycling obligations, circular-economy requirements — Flagged twice: the Indian-economy section cites 'increasing environmental regulations relating to plastic waste management and recycling', and the threats paragraph warns such requirements 'may necessitate additional investments and operational adjustments' - i.e. a potential forced-capex and compliance-cost risk on a plastics-chain business.
- Currency risk on imported inputs, capital equipment and exports — The MD&A says volatility in currency markets 'may impact the cost of imported raw materials and influence export competitiveness', and the Directors' Report cites a 'weakening rupee' among the pressures behind cost optimization. Note 49 states the exposure 'relates primarily to the import of raw materials and spare parts, capital expenditure, exports of finished products', with unhedged USD and Euro trade receivable/payable balances outstanding at the reporting date and a stated 1% sensitivity on profit before tax; the Company says it negotiates derivative terms to match hedged exposures where a hedge is entered into.
- Credit risk from extended customer credit terms — 'The Company faces credit risk through its extended credit terms to customers, which may result in payment delays or defaults.' Mitigations are unusually specific: regular monitoring of receivables and proactive collection, a credit-evaluation policy setting a limit per customer, bank guarantee / letter of credit / security deposit backing where credit risk is assessed as high, expected-credit-loss provisioning on a provision matrix, and - materially - 'all domestic and export sales are protected by a receivable insurance policy'. Trade receivables are stated to consist of a large number of customers.
- Liquidity and interest-rate risk — Liquidity risk is described as the potential inability to meet short-term obligations from insufficient cash flow or limited access to financing, managed through cash-flow forecasting, maintained credit lines and working-capital optimisation across inventory, receivables and payables. On interest rates, Note 49 states market risk 'arises from the Company's use of interest bearing financial instruments' and that the instruments affected are borrowings; the borrowing table shows the reporting-date position as entirely floating-rate INR with no fixed-rate and no foreign-currency borrowing, and the Company discloses a 100 bps sensitivity - so the whole borrowing book reprices with rates.
- Regulatory / statutory change and cyber risk — Regulatory risk from changes in statutes, laws and regulations is managed through periodic legal-compliance reviews and an enterprise-wide compliance management system. Cyber risk - data breaches, cyber attacks or system failures - is addressed with a data-protection policy, encryption and firewalls, and information stored across multiple secure locations. Both sit under the Risk Management Committee, to which the Board has delegated review of the risk-management system in line with the Companies Act 2013 and SEBI Regulations.
- Supplier dependence, partially offset by long-term supply arrangements — The only 'Operational Issues' disclosure in the MD&A risk section is the mitigation itself: 'The Company has long term raw material supply MOU's and majority suppliers of the Company are regular in nature.' No supplier count, no concentration percentage and no named supplier is given, so the residual concentration cannot be sized from the report.
- Indirect-tax disputes outstanding — Back-filled from the sibling capex_expansion bundle: Note 37 'Claims against the Company not acknowledged as debts' carries an 'Excise and Goods and Service Tax matter under dispute' covering show-cause notices for CHA and C&F agents, Cenvat / service tax on sales commission, service-tax credit on sales commission for export sales, GST cross charge and export obligation. Amounts are deliberately not reproduced; the note is truncated after this single row.
